title: Finite-coefficient derived comparison in intrinsic constant-ring coordinates
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme and $B$ a finite commutative ring. Use the small etale/pro-etale sites and specified comparison inverse image $\nu_T^*$ on fixed-$B$ module sheaves of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], and sheafification of [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Let $B_T$ be the constant commutative ring sheaf on the small pro-etale site, the sheafification of the constant presheaf with value $B$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. In the small-site size convention, coefficients and module values are lifted from universe $u$ to $u+1$. Realize a fixed-$B$ module sheaf as a module over $B_T$ by keeping its module presheaf and applying associated-module-sheafification along the constant-scalar unit $B\to B_T$. Compose this realization with the specified comparison inverse image on etale module sheaves. Define the intrinsic finite-coefficient derived comparison $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},B)\to D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_T))$ to be the functor obtained by applying this additive exact comparison termwise to complexes and localizing at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. This specifies the canonical functor, with no constructibility, full-faithfulness or essential-surjectivity assertion.
